simple.meaning: לֶקֶשׁ (leqesh) is a Hebrew word meaning “the after crop.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: לֶקֶשׁ (H3954) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Amos 7:1, with occurrences in Amos.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לֶקֶשׁ (H3954) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in לֶקֶשׁ (H3954) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: לֶקֶשׁ (leqesh) / H3954 is traced through Amos 7:1 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and behold, he formed locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and behold, it was the latter growth after the king’s harvest.

definitions.full: H3954. leqesh לֶ֫קֶשׁ noun [masculine] probably after-growth, after-math , i.e. spring-crop (compare GASm 12Proph. i. 109 ); — only (2 t.) Amos 7:1 , הַמֶּלֶךְ׃ נִּזֵּי אַחַר לֶקֶשׁ וְהִנֵּה הַלָּ֑קֶשׁ עֲלוֺת בִּתְחִלַּת . — > Other interpretations are: late-rain growth (from מַלְקוֺשׁ q. v.), Hoffm ZAW iii. (1883) 116 ; leaf-and-herb-gathering in spring, We after Klein ZPV iv. 1881, 83 ; Anderlind viii. 1886, 62 .
